decisions.reason: As an award-backed yogurt close to our cultured-dairy core, it is still relatively cheap to keep, though after several quiet years we would retain it only while monitoring contribution closely.
After several years without clear evidence of strategic traction, this semi-hard cheese no longer offers enough unresolved upside to justify continued assortment complexity.
The spicy cheese line adds multiple variants in a more niche taste segment, and by now the learning value of keeping that option open is likely outweighed by the cost of carrying it.
This mild creamy soft cheese fits a broad consumer taste and complements our existing cheese range, so it remains worth keeping if its economics stay acceptable.
Washed-rind soft cheese targets a narrower audience, and with uncertainty largely resolved its option value is low compared with reallocating resources to stronger core products or new development.
